newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors close Intel calls.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors close Intel calls.

text.p: Investors swarmed to Intel Corp options as they fled the stock after the company warned of an earnings shortfall for its second quarter, traders said Friday.
Options traders said much of the activity was from investors closing out positions on the call side.

"We had a lot of people who were in buy-writes, where they were long the stock and short the calls," one brokerage firm trader said. "So they're just looking at it right now as an opportune time to buy the calls back."
By about 1000 CDT/1500 GMT, Intel was down 14-1/64 at 149-3/4 on heavy volume of more than 26 million shares.
The stock had reached an intraday low of 137-7/8 after the company said its revenues and net income for the second quarter will fall below expectations because of weaker than projected demand.
The news led to at least one downgrade. Morgan Stanley lowered its opinion on Intel to outperform from strong buy.
Among the options, Intel held the top 10 most active options for calls and six of the top 10 spots on the put side at the American Stock Exchange (AMEX).
The most active Intel options included the June 155 call with turnover of nearly 6,800 contracts, the June 150 call with about 5,140 and the June 145 put with 4,745.
One trader at a brokerage firm in Chicago said his firm had been a small lot buyer of some Intel calls.
"Most of it is covering stuff that we had sold, just covering it off," he said, adding that the firm had been fairly active in the technology sector overall.
Intel calls were busy through the July and October series into the January 1998 series.
Volatilities on Intel options were up but not dramatically so, despite the sharp drop in the stock.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said volatility was in the 36 to 37 range, up from around 32 in April and a 1997 average of 35.
The first trader said some investors took the selloff in Intel, which dragged down many other high tech shares, as an opportunity to get into some other names.
"We've got some big players in 3Com and Cisco, just buying on the weakness of Intel," he said, also citing Dell Computer Corp as another beneficiary.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, options on shares of Cisco were fairly busy, with the heaviest action in the June 65 calls, which traded about 13,700 contracts.
Patrick Hamilton of LETCO said two investors accounted for most of that volume and were sellers of the options.
"I don't know if they were closing or opening (positions), but I think it was an opportunity to sell June 65 volatility at a higher level than it normally would be," he said.
He said volatility, in the mid-30s Thursday, went up to the low 40s as Cisco shares fell, but then eased back toward 40 as the stock recovered.
